May 2024: readiness to arrest Israeli leaders

On Tuesday, 21 May 2024, Norway became the first European country to publicly announce that it would arrest Israeli Prime Minister [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]] and Defense Minister [[yoav-gallant|Yoav Gallant]] if the Hague Tribunal issued arrest warrants against them and they landed on Norwegian territory.[{n}] Foreign Minister [[espen-barth-eide|Espen Barth Eide]] made the statement a day after [[international-criminal-court|ICC]] prosecutor [[karim-khan|Karim Khan]]'s announcement, saying that if warrants were issued 'we will be obliged to arrest them,' and that all signatory countries must act on a court decision.[{n}] Israeli coverage treated the pledge as an idle threat, since no Israeli prime minister or defense minister was likely to visit Norway — a country then considered, along with Spain and Ireland, among the most hostile to Israel in Europe, with bilateral relations at an unprecedented low.[{n}] Britain, by contrast, criticized Khan's decision, particularly the equivalence it drew between the Israeli leaders and the [[hamas|Hamas]] leaders [[yahya-sinwar|Yahya Sinwar]], Muhammad Deif and [[ismail-haniyeh|Ismail Haniyeh]].[{n}]
May 2024 arrest warrant applications and European responses

In May 2024, ICC prosecutor [[karim-khan|Karim Khan]] made a dramatic announcement seeking arrest warrants covering Israeli Prime Minister [[benjamin-netanyahu|Benjamin Netanyahu]] and Defense Minister [[yoav-gallant|Yoav Gallant]] alongside [[hamas|Hamas]] leaders.[{n}] [[norway|Norway]] became the first European state to declare unprompted that it would execute any such warrants, while Britain criticized the decision, objecting in particular to the equivalence drawn between the Israeli leaders and [[yahya-sinwar|Yahya Sinwar]], Muhammad Deif and [[ismail-haniyeh|Ismail Haniyeh]].[{n}] France, which had once helped Israel secretly develop a nuclear weapons program, also came forward in support of the warrants.[{n}]

Badlands contributor [[ghostofbasedpatrickhenry|GhostofBasedPatrickHenry]] urged readers hung up on the claim that the ICC was created by [[george-soros|George Soros]] — and therefore illegitimate — to look past that framing, arguing the more important development was that institutions built by the globalist hegemony were being turned against it.[{n}]
